gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology rates its pick, the DS225+, for only 100,000 files hosted in Synology Drive and 10 users. The DS425+ is rated for 500,000 files and 20 users, and the DS925+ for 500,000 files and 80 users; the Drive Client itself is rated for 500,000 files.
standout_why: I compared against the two Synology Drive spec pages ChatGPT cited (synology.com/en-us/dsm/7.4/software_spec/synology_drive and en-global). They give client OS limits, on-demand requirements and a 500,000-file limit per Drive Client. For models they only say the recommended numbers 'vary by Synology model' and send readers to each product's specs. The KB pages, release notes, the 2020 white paper and patchletter in the uncited results are about features, not per-model limits. ChatGPT's answer calls the DS225+ 'Best overall' and the DS425+ the pick 'for growing storage needs', so it treats the difference as drive bays. It never mentions a limit on file count. None of these pages say that 2025 Plus models accept third-party HDDs only from DSM 7.3 onward, or that M.2 pools and cache still need drives on Synology's list.
decides: This splits Synology's 2-bay and 4-bay picks by how many files a freelancer keeps, not by how much storage. A Dropbox account with more than 100,000 files (common for photo, design and code work) is over the DS225+ Drive rating. Synology says going over 'will not block application operations, but may result in longer response time.' At that size the DS425+ (500,000 files, 20 users) is the cheapest Synology model rated for the job, and the DS925+ makes sense when collaborators share it. The DS225+ stays the pick for smaller libraries. The drive policy supports ChatGPT's 'two NAS-rated drives' advice on DSM 7.3 or later, which allows third-party HDDs and 2.5" SATA SSDs for storage pools on 2025 Plus models. That allowance does not cover the DS425+/DS925+ M.2 slots. QNAP's Qsync does have on-demand files (Space-Saving Mode), which fills a 'Not found' cell on our page. UGREEN's DH-series NAS can't take the Nextcloud-in-Docker route, so that row's 'any x86 NAS' wording should exclude them.

findings.label: Synology Drive maximum hosted files / maximum users
findings.note: Spec text: '100,000 (applies to files indexed or hosted by Synology Drive. For file access through other standard protocols, refer to the File Services section above)'. The user count assumes 20% of users doing file operations and 80% idle. Footnote: 'Exceeding the recommended numbers above will not block application operations, but may result in longer response time.' Tested on Btrfs with non-encrypted shared folders.

findings.label: Synology Drive maximum hosted files / maximum users
findings.note: Same footnotes as the DS225+. 500,000 / 100,000 = 5× the DS225+ file rating, with the same Celeron J4125 and 2 GB RAM (max 6 GB, one slot, D4NS01-4G).

findings.label: Synology Drive maximum hosted files / maximum users
findings.note: The spec page covers both DS925+ and DS925neo+. RAM is 4 GB, expandable to 32 GB (16 GB × 2). Compatible DS925+ modules: D4ES04-4G / D4ES03-8G / D4ES03-16G. Synology says multi-module configurations must use identical modules.

findings.label: Synology Drive Client file limit per client
findings.source_title: Synology Drive Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: The page says exceeding this 'can reduce performance and cause unexpected errors'. It gives no per-model numbers and refers readers to product specs. This is the page ChatGPT cited.

findings.label: Synology Drive Client and On-demand Sync OS requirements and exclusions
findings.value: Client: Windows 10 2004+ (not Windows on ARM or Windows Server), macOS 12+, Ubuntu 20.04+; mobile app iOS 18+ / Android 10+. On-demand: Windows 10 1809+ or macOS 12.3+
findings.source_title: Synology Drive Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: On-demand exclusions: a folder already used by OneDrive Files On-Demand, iCloud Drive or another On-demand task can't be used, and neither can drive roots or user home directories. Windows clients are limited to 64 sync tasks, and .pst files aren't supported. File locking needs clients 4.0.0 or later. Drive Server 3.0+ needs clients 3.0+.

findings.label: Third-party drive policy on 2025 Plus models
findings.value: From DSM 7.3, non-validated third-party drives can be installed and used to create storage pools. M.2 storage pools and cache still require drives on Synology's compatibility list.
findings.source_title: Synology Releases DiskStation Manager 7.3 | Synology Inc.
findings.note: Press release dated October 8, 2025. It covers '25 model year DiskStation Plus, Value, and J series running DSM 7.3'. Footnote 1: 'Creation of M.2 based storage pool and cache still requires drives on the HCL.'

findings.label: M.2 slot use and compatible SSDs
findings.value: 2 × M.2 2280 NVMe; Synology-verified SSDs required for M.2 storage pools (Synology lists SNV3410-400G, SNV5420-400G/800G/1600G); M.2 slots not hot-swappable
findings.note: Spec text: 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'. The DS225+ spec lists no M.2 slots.

findings.label: RAM expansion and compatible module
findings.value: 2 GB preinstalled; max 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB), one slot; compatible module D4NS01-4G
findings.note: Synology: 'will not provide complete product warranty or technical support if non-Synology memory modules are used'. Synology Photos object recognition needs at least 4 GB.

findings.label: Qsync on-demand files (Space-Saving Mode) requirements
findings.value: Qsync Client 5.0.0 or later; Windows 10 version 1909+ or macOS 10.14+
findings.note: Spec text: 'Files are synchronized from the NAS to your devices only when needed.' Sync is supported on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu; backup on Windows and macOS only. This replaces the 'Not found' in our page's QNAP on-demand cell.

findings.label: EZ Sync desktop client builds
findings.note: Windows note: 'For NAS devices running ADM 3.5, please use AES 1.0.6.8290.' The Mac client exists, so our page's 'Windows per Asustor's help' cell is out of date.

findings.label: EZ Sync for Mac ADM requirement and limitation
findings.value: Recommended with ADM 4.3.2 or later; Cloud ID connection not supported in the first Mac release
findings.source_title: Release Notes - Desktop Apps - ASUSTOR NAS
findings.note: AES 1.0.0.100200 (2024-11-06) was a beta: 'All new AES recommended to be used with ADM 4.3.2 or above'. Known limitation: 'Cluod ID connection is not supported' (Asustor's spelling). 1.0.1.100680 (2025-07-14) added WebRelay connection and auto-reconnect after a NAS reboot.

findings.label: Docker availability (route for Nextcloud)
findings.value: DH2300 does not officially support Docker; Docker runs on the DH4300 Plus and DXP models (DXP2800, DXP4800 Plus, DXP4800 Pro, DXP2800 GT, DXP4800 GT, DXP6800 Pro, DXP8800 Plus, DXP480T Plus)
findings.source_title: UGREEN NAS Software and UGOS Pro FAQs
findings.note: The same page says there is no Linux desktop client (use a browser, SMB or NFS) and that only DXP models support Virtual Machine Manager. Our Nextcloud row says 'any x86 NAS'; DH models are ARM, and the DH2300 has no official Docker.
